The *Catutthanaya Saṅgahitenasaṅgahitapadaniddesa* ("Exposition of the Fourth Method: What Is Unincluded by That Which Is Included") constitutes the fourth analytical chapter of the *Dhātukathā*, the third treatise of the canonical Theravāda *Abhidhamma Piṭaka* [SuttaCentral]. In keeping with the analytical methodology of the *Dhātukathā*, the text interrogates doctrinal items in terms of their inclusion and non-inclusion within the overarching categories of aggregates (*khandha*), bases (*āyatana*), and elements (*dhātu*). SuttaCentral records one translation of the work [SuttaCentral].

It shares extensive textual segments with the third method (*Tatiyanaya*, Dt 2.3), the eleventh method (*Ekādasamanaya*, Dt 2.11), the fifth method (*Pañcamanaya*, Dt 2.5), the fourteenth method (*Cuddasamanaya*, Dt 2.14), and other chapters, as well as with the *Abhidhammamātikāpāḷi*, the *Paṭiccasamuppādavibhaṅga* (Vb 6), and the Abhidhamma sub-commentarial literature (*Pañcapakaraṇa-mūlaṭīkā* and *Pañcapakaraṇa-anuṭīkā*) [DharmaNexus].
